subject: elephant
pitch: A gentle African elephant calf. Wrinkly slate-grey skin with a dusty, reddish tint from rolling in the dirt, huge fan-shaped ears with a pink flush on the inside, a curious trunk curling forward, stubby baby tusks, long lashes over kind brown eyes, a little tufted tail and round, padded feet with pale toenails.
reasoning:
I'm planning out an elephant calf model using the SDK, sizing it around 1 meter at the shoulder, facing forward with left side to +X, and sketching the body structure as a spine chain or loft from hips to shoulders.

Now I'm working out the joint hierarchy -- a root hip joint, then a spine chain through several control points up to the chest, figuring out how the chain naming and joint parenting should work along the path.

Still structuring the skeleton joints...

Placing the head joint at the neck's tip, parented to neck1, with a forward-upward direction so the bone runs from neck to head naturally.

For the head geometry itself, I'm using a sphere part attached to the head bone, specifying an explicit position so it sits at the top of the neck rather than defaulting to the joint location.

For the ears, I'm extruding fan-shaped outlines positioned on either side of the head, working out the plane orientation (forward/up directions and normal) so the thin ear slab faces outward correctly, then sketching a rounded fan outline sized for a calf's proportionally large ears.

For the inner ear detail, I'm considering a simpler approach: a small pink slab layered on top of the outer ear outline, offset slightly outward, rather than trying to mottle or gradient-paint the single ear shape.

For skin, I'm settling on a mottled paint mixing slate and dusty reddish-brown tones at a moderate grain size for texture.

For the trunk, I'm sketching it as a chain of segments curling forward and downward from the head, tapering as it goes, though I need to figure out the right role designation since there's no dedicated "trunk" option—maybe "tail" works as a stand-in.

I'm deciding to use a tapering sweep along the trunk chain, with radius shrinking from base to tip, and considering adding a small sphere at the very end to cap it, while working out which joint name to anchor that tip piece to given how the chain's joints are indexed.

For attachment, I'm figuring out that the trunk's first joint should parent to the head joint since it's closest to the trunk's starting point, and I'll set that explicitly rather than relying on auto-detection. Then I'm moving on to the tusks, planning to build them as short stubby cream-colored cones projecting forward from the head using the spike helper, positioning their base points symmetrically and angling them slightly outward and downward.

Now I'm working out the eyes and lashes: small dark spheres placed symmetrically on the sides of the head, with a handful of thin rod-shaped lashes curving up and outward from the top of each eye to give it some character. After that I'm sketching out the tail as a tapering chain of three joints running from the pelvis backward and downward, using a sweep that narrows from a thicker base to a thin tip, with a tuft planned at the end.

Now I'm figuring out the leg structure — four legs, each needing a hip-to-knee-to-ankle chain with proper joint naming so the limb bends correctly, plus a separate foot piece at the tip, and working through how many path points and names are needed to get the tip joint to land exactly at the ankle.

I'm setting leg thickness with a tapered radius from hip to ankle, placing hips and knees at approximate body-relative coordinates, and planning rounded, slightly flattened feet positioned at ground level with toenail details for the front legs.

For the toenails I'll use small pale spheres scaled flat near the front of each foot, keeping it simple with three per foot rather than repeating full leg definitions four separate times — using a loop with unique joint names per leg instead.

Now I'm working out the body loft stations, adjusting the torso's center height and radius so the shoulder and back proportions look right without making the body too tall.

I'm placing the neck and head position, sizing the head as a scaled sphere to get calf-like proportions, then figuring out ear placement — flared outward from the skull at an angle, sized fairly large and flat, attached to the head bone.

For coloring the ear, I'm thinking through which face should show the pink inner-ear tint versus the outer grey skin: since the ear curls, the inner-facing surface (normal pointing back toward the head) should get the pink paint while the rest stays the base skin tone, using a normal-based paint function to distinguish the two faces.

For the eyes, I'll keep it simple with a dark brown sphere plus a tiny white highlight sphere, and skip detailed trunk wrinkles or nostril texture for now.

For the body skin, I'm settling on a mottled grey-brown paint with moderate contrast and patch size rather than trying to combine mottle with countershading, since nesting those paint functions adds unnecessary complexity.

Now I'm working out positions: pale toenails, dark lash rods, and placing the eyes relative to the head sphere so they sit just inside the front surface without clipping through the ears. I'm also planning the tusks as spike primitives angled outward and downward from the mouth, with a cream tusk color, and considering whether to add a separate jaw joint and lower jaw part so the mouth could open, per the build guidelines about articulated mouths.

For the body, I'm deciding to use a loft along a spine chain running from the hips to the chest rather than binding it rigidly to root, so the torso can bend naturally, and I'm thinking through how the leg bones will attach at the hips off that same chain.

Working out the joint positions and parenting for front and hind legs relative to the spine chain...

Defining leg sweep geometry...

Now I'm working through the skeleton hierarchy for the neck and head joints, making sure the head joint parents correctly off the neck and that a sweep covers the neck tube between body and head. Then I'm starting the trunk chain, positioning its origin just in front of the head so it extends outward correctly.

Still building the chain geometry...

For the tail tuft I'm adding a dark brown sphere plus a few spikes at the tip, then moving to the eyes — small spheres for sclera, white highlight dots, and thin rod lashes angled outward from each eye, before starting work on the ears.

Now I'm shaping the ear as a flat extruded outline, a rounded blob with a drooping lower flap, tilting its orientation outward to flare naturally from the head.

I'm positioning each ear's origin at the side of the head so its outline spans the right z-range, then painting the inner surface pink based on normal direction while leaving the outer side skin-colored, using a per-point color function fed into the extrude mesh.

For the head, I'm applying a non-uniform scale to the sphere geometry and keeping the skin paint consistent across head, body, and spine parts, layering in mottling and a dustier reddish tint toward the lower body and legs for texture rather than explicit wrinkle geometry. I'm wrapping up with the shadow and dust color constants, the export metadata naming this "African elephant calf," and starting the builder setup.

Setting up joint hierarchy...

I'm connecting the head joint to the neck chain's end point, then setting up a sweep for the neck tapering from the base to the head radius. Then I'm working through the leg chains, naming joints like upperFL/lowerFL/footFL and assigning parents (spine2 for front legs, spine1 for hind legs) to match the chain options schema.

Now I'm figuring out the leg sweeps with a tapering radius function, then placing the foot pads and toenails relative to each ankle position -- offsetting pad centers downward and forward, and positioning nail geometry at the front edge of each foot sphere based on front vs. hind leg z-coordinates.

I'm also adding the tail tuft as a small sphere at the tail's end bone, placing the eye highlights, and starting to lay out the full component file with color constants and the builder setup.

Writing component setup code...

Verifying chain weighting resolves to the root joint when points coincide with the spine's base, and confirming the head sphere attaches rigidly to the head bone using its explicit bone option and placement vector.

Now I'm designing the trunk as a curling chain of points from the head down toward the ground, sweeping it with a radius that tapers from base to tip, then capping the tip with a small sphere parented to the final trunk joint.

Next I'm adding tusks as spikes curving down from the head, then building the eyes as small spheres with highlight dots, and generating lashes as thin rods curling outward from each eye edge.

For the ears, I'm extruding a flat outline shape, positioning it on the side of the head with a tilt so the top flares outward, checking that the orientation vectors and thickness keep it anchored near the skull surface while angling away realistically.

I'm figuring out the right ear offset so the base stays tucked against the head while the top leans outward beyond the head's curved profile, then using a normal-based paint rule to shade the inner pink surface of the ear. Now I'm moving to leg definitions, setting up a data array for front-left, front-right, hind-left, and hind-right legs with their mirrored x-sign values to drive hip/knee/ankle placement.

I'm placing hip, knee, and ankle joints for front and hind legs, then chaining them into upper/lower/foot segments parented to the appropriate spine joint, adjusting hind-leg parenting since it sits closer to spine1. I'm also tapering the leg sweep radius and nudging the hip x-position inward slightly so the legs don't poke too far past the body's loft width.

Now I'm shaping the paw geometry: adding a flattened sphere for each foot pad and three small nail spheres along the front edge, then checking the math so the nails sit just at or slightly past the pad's front surface rather than floating inside it.

Next I'm building the tail as a two-segment chain with a tapering sweep, a dark fur tuft sphere at the tip, and three downward-angled spikes radiating from that tip for texture. Then I'm starting on the neck chain.

I'm working out the neck's attachment point, realizing the spine chain's last point isn't itself a joint but serves as the implicit parent location for the neck's first segment, so the neck connects correctly at spine2's end. I'm sweeping the neck with a tapering radius and starting to define the head joint based on the neck's direction vector.

Now I'm checking the overall joint hierarchy order—spine, neck, head, jaw, then trunk and tusks branching off the head, with legs attached to the spine—making sure everything builds in the right sequence. I'm positioning the jaw joint and its box geometry against the head sphere, computing the head's radius at that height to make sure the jaw box protrudes naturally from the face, and now I'm calculating where the trunk base should sit relative to the head's front surface.

I'm recalculating eye placement since the eyes were sitting slightly inside the head surface rather than on it—using the ellipsoid equation to find the correct z-depth so the eyes sit just outside the skull at the proper angle, then adjusting tusk base coordinates the same way so they emerge naturally from the jaw surface rather than floating or clipping through it. Now I'm working out ear placement using the same surface-fitting approach.

I'm checking the body loft stations to make sure the rump, torso, and chest proportions line up correctly with leg and head heights so nothing clips or floats, then verifying each builder API call (loft, sweep, rod, spike, extrude, paint) against its expected type signature to catch any mismatches before finalizing. I'm also designing a wrinkle/mottle paint function that layers noise-based color variation with contour-line wrinkles for a more textured hide, then assembling all these pieces into the final model code.
